pr_body:
Implement `crdb_internal.stream_partition` builtin to emit
partition data during replication streaming.

Fixes #70924

Release Notes: None
pr_comments: This change is [](https://reviewable.io/reviews/cockroachdb/cockroach/73685)

Only the top commit is about stream_partition builtin.  The rest of the code is being reviewed in https://github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/pull/71672

Keeping this as a draft PR since I want to expand test coverage for this code; but I think it's a good first start.
Please comment, let me know if you see any glaring issues.
@yuzefovich mind taking a look at the first commit (avoid_buffering session var)?
Ack; good point re compression - -I forget we're not running under grpc here... But, as you say, we have options, so going to keep it simple for now.
@yuzefovich Looks like backing out those few changes still has CI clean.

issue_context.title: changefeedccl: Implement partition streaming primitive
issue_context.body:
Implement crdb_internal.crdb_internal.stream_partition(streamID, spec) as described in
https://docs.google.com/document/d/1i7x6ce0SGMbJ3KEszeRVjRS0LaPhxulcUbi029nVy7c/edit#

A function takes a stream ID (just a job id), verifies if the job is running, and a "spec" -- information necessary to start
the flow to emit all KVs for the specified partition.

Epic CRDB-6407

review_comments:
I'm trying to figure out if I think we should be boxing these bytes in another proto, to add any sort of versioning or anything, leave room for a compression-identifying header or whatever.

I suppose we could just say that the passed spec would ask for a particular stream version / encoding / compression / etc that it expects to decode and then this producer is just obligated to either produce what is requested or refuse with an error, so then don't need to worry about it identifying what we produced in the produced data?

so just leaving this as a naked marshaled proto would be okay?

I don't really have much expertise in the sql session / serialize session / exec stuff -- my weak preference would be to split out the avoid buffering bits to their own PR that someone on SQL could stamp too, but it's a weak preference.

Yeah; I spoke w/ Yahor on this.  I just want to have this together w/ the use case for this setting.
@yuzefovich do you mind taking a peak at the AvoidBuffering bit?
I don't really understand why we have all these hooks and mutable function pointers in the ccl code.
yeah, I think we need to clean this up.  There should be just 1 hook to set the manager.  Though, maybe the issue was w/ circular dependencies on jobs package? @gh-casper do you remember?
this feels like it needs to call `checkPrivilegedUser` right?
Yeah; looks like we have to do it for all calls here.  I'm going to address this in another PR.
